findings.source_passage: He was such a creature as civilized, domestic people in the temperate zone only see in their dreams, and that but dimly
findings.why_it_matters: The source's exact phrasing — 'civilized, domestic people in the temperate zone' — is a rhetorically precise formulation central to the chapter's contrast between modernity and primal antiquity; the draft reduces it to 'temperate, domestic folk,' losing the word 'civilized' and the deliberate irony packed into it.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'civilized, domestic people in the temperate zone only see in their dreams, and that but dimly' verbatim or near-verbatim.

findings.source_passage: those insulated, immemorial, unalterable countries, which even in these modern days still preserve much of the ghostly aboriginalness of earth's primal generations, when the memory of the first man was a distinct recollection
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'the memory of the first man was a distinct recollection' is interpretively crucial — it positions Fedallah within a theological-anthropological timescale that underpins the novel's metaphysics; the draft paraphrases it away entirely, collapsing it to 'where earth's ghostly aboriginalness lingers.'
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'the memory of the first man was a distinct recollection, and all men his descendants, unknowing whence he came, eyed each other as real phantoms' — this clause is too interpretively loaded to flatten.

findings.source_passage: So Tamerlane's soldiers often argued with tears in their eyes, whether that invaluable life of his ought to be carried into the thickest of the fight.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Among whale-wise people it has often been argued'
findings.why_it_matters: The Tamerlane analogy is Melville's signature mode of aggrandizing Ahab through historical-military parallel; its complete omission erases an important layer of epic register that the critical tradition consistently marks as Melville's heroic-ironic framing of Ahab.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Tamerlane comparison, even in abbreviated form: 'So Tamerlane's soldiers argued with tears whether that invaluable life ought to enter the thickest of the fight.'

findings.source_passage: Beelzebub himself might climb up the side and step down into the cabin to chat with the captain, and it would not create any unsubduable excitement in the forecastle.
findings.source_locator: paragraph on subordinate phantoms, 'wonders soon wane'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves the gist but drops 'with the captain,' softening the specific comic image of Beelzebub having a cozy captain's-cabin chat; the rhythm and specificity are signature Melville deadpan.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'to chat with the captain' to preserve the exact comic register.

summary: Three medium-severity failures — erasure of the Tamerlane analogy, flattening of the 'civilized, domestic people in the temperate zone' formulation, and loss of 'the memory of the first man was a distinct recollection' — together constitute sufficient grounds for regeneration.
